question.problem:
Let $(v,w)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $v+w?$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.4v-2w=2 \\ v-w=1\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the top equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.4v-2w=2 & |\,\times 10 \\ v-w=1 & \end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}4v-20w=20 \\ v-w=1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we multiply the second equation by $-4,$ then we will get a $-4v$ term that can cancel with the $4v$ term in the first equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4v-20w=20 &  \\ v-w=1 & |\,\times (-4)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}4v-20w=20 \\ -4v+4w=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $v$-variable and allows us to solve for $w:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{4v}-20w & =20 \\ -\cancel{4v}+4w & =-4 \\ (-20w+4w) & =(20-4) \\ -16w & =16 \\ w & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $w=-1$ into the equation $v-w=1$ to solve for $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v-w & =1 \\ v-(-1) & =1 \\ v+1 & =1 \\ v & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $v=0,\,w=-1.$ So,

$$
v+w=0+(-1)=-1.
$$
